content.text: Finalise van design
Complete design.
Finalise cabinet doors and door hardware.
Finalise bed.
Finalise drawer.
Finalise floor; investigate using two pieces of plywood.
Find Twin Peaks zig-zag floor vinyl.
Design how the interior fixes to the van.
Refine measurements.

Scan and measure the actual NV200 using Dot3D on the iPhone, inspect and assemble the geometry in CloudCompare on Windows, then rebuild the vehicle in our campervan app. The goal is the closest practical model, followed by final measurements and templates for fitted woodwork.
Complete the rear-corner sample through export and inspection before capturing the full van.
Set up the iPhone, Windows software and scan folder
Use the iPhone 14 Pro Max for capture and Dot3D optimisation. Use the Windows PC with the RTX 3080 for CloudCompare. A Dot3D Windows licence is not needed for this route.
Item
Use / source
iPhone 14 Pro Max
Existing phone; rear LiDAR and camera
Dot3D Pro or active all-access trial
Capture, reference distances, optimisation and E57 export
CloudCompare, Windows 64-bit
Free; official download link in the next substep
Printed Dot3D targets, painter’s tape, flat card if needed
Black-and-white printing at a library or copy shop; keep the coded area uncovered
Steel tape measure and straight ruler
Measure target centres; use the ruler where the tape hook would obscure an endpoint
Blender
Optional mesh viewing; CloudCompare can inspect the results
Install Dot3D and enable capture plus exports
Install Dot3D from its App Store link on the
official download page

. Start the seven-day all-access trial when ready to make the sample capture, or use an active Pro licence. Free mode after the trial has no exports. For a website-issued licence key, the documented entry point is Settings → About → License Info. Instructions:
Dot3D activation
Install CloudCompare on Windows. Download the stable Windows 64-bit installer from
CloudCompare
Prepare the actual surfaces that the furniture must fit
Expose the cargo body where accessible

Remove loose gear, bedding and removable obstructions from the cargo area. Expose both wheel arches, the rear sill and pillars, sliding-door posts, lower wall returns, cab-end floor boundary and roof rails/bows where accessible.

Record any existing lining, flooring or fixed fitting that still hides metal. Add a photograph and a missing-coverage note for each concealed area. Capture the visible layer and identify it in the notes; a hidden surface needs later access or a separate measurement.
Identify the floor reference and the existing CAD convention
Use an identifiable metal floor level, noting whether it is a rib crest, recess or another fixed reference. Photograph the spot used for height measurements.

Our app uses millimetres: X goes from vehicle left/passenger side to right/driver side, Y goes from the rear opening toward the cab, and Z goes up. Y = 0 is the rear opening at its side pillars. Z = 0 is the finished plywood floor; the current metal floor is Z = −18 mm (
floor_build_up_mm = 18
). Record the measured floor build-up so the assistant can apply the correct offset later.

Current model references on 28 October 2026: cargo width 1500 mm, body length 1900 mm, body height 1347 mm, wheel-arch height 280 mm and slat-top height 390 mm above finished floor. Keep these as the existing CAD reference values; record the actual van dimensions alongside them.
Capture the furniture fitting surfaces

Prioritise the wheel-arch tops and ends, lower side walls behind the long bench and cabinet, rear-pillar curves, both sliding-door openings, cab-end cross-bench support area, and the roof/rail surfaces that limit cabinet height.
Photograph narrow lips and recesses that the phone cannot capture clearly. Measure their depth or thickness separately where accessible.
Print and place the AprilTags
Keep each tag flat; attach it to flat card if the paper would curl. Leave the black pattern and surrounding margin visible.
Attach fixed references around the cargo body

Start with the rear and cab-end locations in the table, spread along the van and at different heights. Tape the paper edges securely without covering the pattern. Use fixed bodywork and returns for references. Keep those targets in the same position until all captures and checks are complete.
Provide shared references between separate captures

Arrange at least three common stationary tags wherever two captures will overlap, including near an opening connecting the interior and exterior. Spread the common tags across different surfaces/heights. Plan the capture path so all shared tags are detected in each relevant scan.
Keep sliding doors and the rear hatch out of the shared-reference system because their positions change between captures.
Instructions:
Dot3D shared-tag registration
Check that the phone detects the tags

Use a short sample capture to confirm that tag IDs register. The official quick guide shows detected tags turning orange; some versions show a yellow outline. If a tag is not detected, adjust its viewing angle, lighting or flatness.
Keep the whole pattern in view and use the available stand-off inside the van. The vendor advises avoiding tag capture closer than roughly 600 mm where possible.
Instructions:
Tag detection
Measure constraints and keep independent check distances

Fill the table before optimising a scan. The proposed pairs below identify physical locations; replace the location descriptions with the actual printed tag IDs. Add rows if additional captures need their own references.

Instructions:
Measured distances in optimisation
Measure each accessible input pair twice

Read the straight-line distance between the two circled centres. Keep the tape straight and supported. A path around an obstacle or following the body curve is a different distance and cannot be entered as that target pair.

Write both readings in millimetres. If they disagree beyond what you can reliably read, repeat the measurement and fix the cause before using the value. Record the spread of your repeat readings as the measurement uncertainty.
Replace any inaccessible pair

If a proposed pair has no clear straight measuring path, choose another pair covering a similar direction and update the table. The exact same endpoints must be present in the scan. Use at least one useful long reference and distribute other references across the cargo area and heights.
Measure the independent checks without entering them into Dot3D

Use the C rows for distances that are separate from all input constraints. Photograph non-tag endpoints with a ruler or a small visible mark. Include several parts of the van so a local error cannot hide behind one correct overall length.
Keep C01–C05 out of the optimisation inputs for the version being assessed. Later we will compare the reconstructed distances with these values.
Record hidden details and the physical floor build-up

Measure accessible rib/lip depths, panel returns and the existing floor layers that the scan cannot resolve. Record exactly which surfaces the measurement touches. If a dimension is inaccessible, mark it “unmeasured” and add it to the later template check.
Run the complete workflow on one rear-corner sample

Use one rear corner containing a wheel arch, adjoining wall and metal floor. This sample establishes that capture, reference-distance entry, E57 transfer, CloudCompare inspection and a usable reference mesh work before the full session.
Start a sample scan with stable geometry and fixed tags in view
In Dot3D choose New Scan. Frame the floor, wall and rear-corner geometry together until the green Scene Fitness indicator is near full. Name the capture
nv200-rear-corner-sample-01
. Start with the capture button, then move steadily around the accessible corner.
Instructions:
Start and finish capture
Capture the whole sample and return to its starting references

Include the wheel-arch crown, front and rear ends, wall transition and adjacent floor from different viewpoints. Keep the doors fixed throughout. Revisit the starting tags before stopping with the capture button.
Save the unoptimised sample as a separate DP file
Choose File → Save as, select DP, continue with OKAY, choose the destination and SAVE SCENE. Use
nv200-rear-corner-sample-01-raw.dp
. Keep this copy so the capture can be processed again.
Instructions:
DP saving
Add the sample’s measured input distances and optimise

Open Targets, then Reference Distances; the vendor’s other illustrated guide calls the creation control New Ref. Distance. Select the two recognised tag IDs, enter their measured separation in the units shown, and confirm the entry. Repeat only for input pairs visible in this sample.
For example, a recorded 1500 mm distance is 1.500 if the dialog shows metres. Review every pair and unit before proceeding. The grey preview is the raw estimate.
Instructions:
Reference-distance entry
Choose Optimize on the top bar and then OPTIMIZE SCENE. Retain the automatically selected techniques initially. Save a separate
nv200-rear-corner-sample-01-optimised.dp
Instructions:
Optimisation
Export the sample as E57 and open it on Windows
Choose Share/Export → As Other File → E57 → OKAY, review the output transform and choose EXPORT SCENE. Save to an iPhone Files location that can be transferred to the Windows PC. Copy the E57 to
02-optimised
and both DP copies to
01-originals
02-optimised
as appropriate.
In CloudCompare use File → Open for the E57. Keep the original export and select the imported sample when saving the working BIN project in the next substep.
Instructions:
E57 export
Check the sample scale and independent measurements in CloudCompare

Choose Tools → Point picking and its two-point distance mode. Pick a recorded sample distance and confirm the coordinate unit: a 1500 mm span reads 1.5 in metre coordinates. Save the label and record the unit. Repeat the wheel-arch width and height checks using their photographed endpoints.

Record cloud minus tape for those checks in the measurement table. Save the sample as a CloudCompare BIN file in 03-cloudcompare. Keep the independent checks separate from the target-pair distances used during optimisation.
Instructions:
CloudCompare measurements
Make one reference mesh from the sample

Select the sample cloud. Use Edit → Normals → Compute with Auto neighbourhood size; use valid sensor/grid orientation if available, otherwise Minimum Spanning Tree. Then open Plugins → PoissonRecon with output density as SF enabled and leave the other parameters at their defaults initially.

Inspect the result against the cloud. Use the mesh density display and Edit → Scalar fields → Filter by Value to remove unsupported extensions. Save the resulting sample mesh as OBJ or STL and keep the BIN containing both the cloud and mesh.
If this produces a distorted or closed-over arch, retain the cloud, settings and screenshot for the assistant. Resolve the sample before carrying the same settings over to the full van.
Decide whether to continue with the full capture

Continue when the sample opens at the expected physical scale, its independent distances are recorded, and wheel-arch / floor / wall boundaries are identifiable without doubled surfaces. Record the actual discrepancies.
Capture the full cargo interior with the doors open
Suggested file prefix:
nv200-interior-open-01
. Keep both sliding doors and the rear hatch in fixed open positions for this entire scan. This is the main body reference.
Start at the rear opening with floor, pillar and side wall visible
Choose New Scan and start at the rear corner used in the sample. Confirm the fixed starting tags register. Begin when the Scene Fitness indicator shows a useful view.
Capture the lower body and both wheel arches

From the rear and side openings, sweep the metal floor, both lower side walls, wheel-arch sides/tops/ends, rear sill and pillar bases. Change viewpoint enough to expose the inward returns and recesses. Keep surrounding body features in view when approaching a detail.
Capture the cab-end area and both sliding openings

Include the floor under the cross-bench supports, the transition toward the cab, fixed sliding-door posts, sills, rails and opening returns. Record the positions of existing trim and seats that block a view. Revisit fixed tags as you pass them.
Capture the upper walls and ceiling interfaces
Include the wall taper, roof side rails, exposed bows, rear upper corners and the surfaces above the cabinet. Photograph any deep roof/rail feature that remains unclear.
Close the scan loop and save the raw file
Return to the initial rear-corner view and detect the starting tags again. End capture and save
nv200-interior-open-01-raw.dp
before optimisation.
Fill missed fixed-body areas while the scan is still raw

Inspect the raw preview for holes at the wheel arches, door returns and roof rails. To add coverage, use Scan/Append → Append to this scan, choose a thumbnail showing an unchanged location, and line the camera up with the transparent view until capture resumes. Finish and save another raw version.
Append operates on unoptimised scans. If the scene has changed or you cannot recover the view, create a separately named capture with shared stationary targets.
Instructions:
Append
Record unresolved coverage
Add each remaining hidden or unreliable area to
session-notes.txt
, with a photograph and the associated scan name. Glass and reflections need separate identification; retain the measured window opening and frame as the geometric reference.
Capture the interior surfaces of the closed doors
Suggested file prefix:
nv200-interior-closed-01
. Finish and save the open-door scan before changing any door position. Separate captures preserve each door configuration.
Set the closed-door configuration before starting

Position yourself for the required capture and close the doors before pressing the capture button. Include the stationary body tags and adjoining bodywork visible from inside. Keep every door in that position for the scan.
Capture door panels and their clearance to the fixed body

Capture the inward-most door surfaces, panel bulges, window surrounds and the areas adjacent to the rear drawer / cabinet / bed. Include overlaps with the main body capture so the assistant can place the closed doors accurately.
Finish, save and label the configuration
Save a separate raw DP and note which doors were closed. If a door must move to let you out, end the scan first. Use later separate captures for anything concealed by that movement.
Add an extra door detail capture only where coverage needs it
Use a new file name describing the door and its fixed position. Include adjoining stationary body references if placement is needed. Keep this door geometry separate during alignment and meshing.
Capture the exterior required for the vehicle model
Suggested file prefix:
nv200-exterior-closed-01
. Use the exterior capture for the vehicle shell and the interior capture for furniture clearance.
Establish the closed exterior configuration and reference overlap

Close the sliding doors and rear hatch before starting the exterior scan. Add unique fixed exterior targets as needed. If all useful shared interior references are concealed, plan an additional doors-open bridging capture around an opening; do not assume two non-overlapping scans align automatically.
Capture a continuous exterior loop
Capture the rear, both sides and accessible cab/front surfaces with overlaps, then return to the start. Include fixed body corners and visible reference tags. Keep doors stationary throughout.
Capture accessible roof and opening details

Capture the roof where it is visible from accessible viewpoints. Mark any inaccessible roof surface as a gap. Record approximate glass planes from the surrounding frame and measurements where LiDAR returns are unreliable.
Create a bridging capture if the inside and outside need a shared frame

After saving the closed scan, set the chosen opening to a fixed open position and make a new scan containing interior fixed-body references, jamb/threshold geometry and external fixed-body references. Include at least three common stationary tags for each intended Dot3D link. Label the open door surfaces separately.
Save raw files and record what each capture contributes
Note the exterior and bridge filenames, door positions and shared tag IDs. Preserve separate inner and outer surfaces; their separation is part of the measured body shape.
Optimise each completed capture using its own measured references
Instructions:
Dot3D distance constraints
Instructions:
Dot3D optimisation
Save the final raw version before processing

Finish all intended append passes and use File → Save as to keep the completed unoptimised DP. Use a version suffix when replacing an earlier raw attempt. Keep the raw copy unchanged while working on the result.
Enter every valid input distance visible in this capture

In Targets → Reference Distances / New Ref. Distance, select the two actual recognised tag IDs and enter their separation. Repeat for the I rows present in this scan. Use the units shown in the dialog. Leave the C rows out.
Review constraints before pressing Optimize

Check the ID pair, value, unit and physical endpoints against the measurement record. A grey raw distance can differ from the entered value; a factor of 1000 or an unrelated tag pair needs correction before processing.
Run optimisation and save a new result
Tap Optimize → OPTIMIZE SCENE, initially leaving the detected techniques selected. Wait for completion, inspect the result from top, side and rear views, then save a separately named optimised DP.
Recover from a wrong constraint using the preserved raw copy

If processing bends, splits or stretches the model, reopen the named raw DP, correct the tag pair / units / distance, and optimise again to a new file. Preserve the failed result with a short note so it can be compared if needed.
Check independent distances and decide which capture to retain

Use the C endpoints in the resulting scan and record the reconstructed distance and signed difference: scan minus tape. Check corners and upper/lower regions as well as long spans. If differences vary by location, investigate capture or alignment before applying a global scale change.
For a doubtful region, make a separate repeated capture and compare it against the same checks. Keep the result with better supported geometry and coverage, recording the reason.
Export and archive all useful Dot3D captures
Instructions:
Save the native project
Instructions:
Export E57
Save named raw and optimised DP files
Use File → Save as for each named version. Keep the raw DP in
01-originals
and the optimised DP in
02-optimised
. The native files preserve the Dot3D project for later processing.
Export E57 with consistent output coordinates

For each retained result choose Share/Export → As Other File → E57 → OKAY, review output transform options, then EXPORT SCENE. Use the same output-coordinate convention for captures already registered together. Record any applied transform and the geometry unit in the session notes.
Transfer files to the dated Windows folder
Transfer the E57s and named DP files to the dated Windows folder using iPhone Files and a cloud folder accessible on the PC.
Keep a capture index
File / version
Door positions
Shared fixed tags
Reference inputs
Remaining gaps
interior-open-01
Sliding doors and hatch open
interior-closed-01
Record each door
exterior-closed-01
All captured doors closed
bridge / detail captures
Open and check the point clouds in CloudCompare
Instructions:
File formats
Instructions:
Distance labels
Open the sample first, then the full E57 captures
Choose File → Open and select the sample E57. Expand its entry in the DB tree; E57 may contain several clouds. Once the sample route works, open the retained full captures in the same way.
Confirm the physical coordinate unit

Use Tools → Point picking, choose the two-point distance mode, and pick the endpoints of a recorded reference. Save the distance label. A tape distance near 1500 mm should read near 1.5 if the geometry coordinates are metres.

Record the unit actually observed and check more than one known distance. Keep the scan coordinates in metres during CloudCompare work if that is how the file arrives. We will convert to the app’s millimetres once during import.
Save a CloudCompare working project
Select the imported entities in the DB tree and use File → Save, choosing CloudCompare BIN. Save as
03-cloudcompare/nv200-01-imported.bin
. Keep the E57 originals unchanged.
Create working copies for segmentation
Select the cloud, choose Edit → Clone, rename the copy to describe its region/configuration and hide the original. Keep an untouched import and a separate working entity in the BIN project.
Separate fixed body, doors and unwanted surroundings

Use Edit → Segment on a working cloud. Left-click the polygon, right-click to close it, then choose points inside or outside. Space pauses selection so the view can rotate; inspect from more than one direction. Apply with Return to retain both pieces for inspection.
Name the retained entities
body-interior
body-exterior
door-left-closed
door-right-closed
hatch-closed
, and any open/detail versions that are useful. Remove people, gear and background from the working entities.
Instructions:
Segmentation controls
Record independent measurements before further editing
Check key
Tape, mm
Repeated tape, mm
Cloud, mm
Cloud − tape, mm
Endpoint / coverage notes

Pick the photographed endpoints with the two-point tool and save the labels in BIN. Where a target centre or endpoint cannot be identified reliably in the points, record that limitation and use another marked check.
Align separate captures where they need it

Retain the common coordinates for captures already registered by Dot3D. Use the following procedure only for independently positioned captures. Align fixed body regions before positioning their associated door data.
Instructions:
Point-pair alignment
Choose the stable reference and the moving capture

Select two working body clouds. Choose Tools → Registration → Align (point pairs picking). Assign the main interior as Reference and the other capture as Aligned. Pick at least three well-spread, non-collinear corresponding points in matching order.
Use tag centres only if they are identifiable in the exported points. CloudCompare’s point-pair tool is manual picking; it does not automatically decode AprilTags.
Preview rigid alignment with fixed scale
Keep fixed scale checked. Preview with align, inspect each point-pair error, and correct a mistaken correspondence. Accept with the green tick. Save the transformation report and a BIN checkpoint.
Refine using only overlapping stationary body geometry

If coarse alignment leaves small offsets, select the pair and choose Tools → Registration → Fine registration (ICP). Model is the fixed reference; Data is the capture that moves. Leave Adjust scale off.

Set Final overlap to the estimated proportion of Data that is also present in Model. Use matching fixed-body subsets if most of either capture contains unrelated geometry. Start with other settings at their defaults.
Instructions:
ICP settings
Inspect the alignment away from the picked references
Look for doubled floor ribs, wheel-arch edges, pillar returns and roof features. Compare independent check distances and overlaps at both ends of the van.
Apply the same rigid transform to associated door / detail entities

If alignment used only a fixed-body subset, preserve its transformation report. Apply that same transform to the original associated entities from the same capture through Edit → Apply transformation. Keep door-open and door-closed objects separate.
Save registered clouds before any merge
Save
nv200-02-registered.bin

. Keep named individual clouds. If a combined fixed-body cloud is useful, clone the relevant clouds, choose Edit → Merge, and name the merged result. Merging concatenates the data and does not refine alignment.
Instructions:
Merge behaviour
Clean the working geometry and record the remaining errors
Crop obvious isolated clutter and inspect thin features

Work on copies and remove clearly unrelated points with segmentation. Retain real roof rails, ribs, narrow returns and panel edges. Inspect any automated noise filtering on a small representative region before applying it more widely; record the settings and keep the unfiltered version.
Keep incomplete surfaces identified

Record holes, reflective glass artefacts, inaccessible roof areas and remaining trim in the session notes. Keep inner and outer body surfaces distinguishable. Any later fitted or filled surface must be identifiable as reconstructed rather than directly captured.
Update the independent-check table after alignment and cleanup

Repeat the C measurements using the same endpoints. Record the largest discrepancy and its location as well as the individual values. If cleanup removed an endpoint, use the preserved cloud and record why it is absent from the working copy.
Save the cleaned reference project
Save
nv200-03-cleaned.bin
, retaining reference clouds, working clouds, measured labels and separate doors. Export the cleaned body cloud as E57 or PLY for the handoff alongside BIN.
Create and inspect the reference mesh
Start with the rear-corner sample. Create separate meshes for body-interior, body-exterior and each door configuration so their openings and nearby surfaces remain distinct.
Instructions:
Poisson reconstruction and density trimming
Select a working cloud and compute its normals
Normals are local surface-direction arrows used by reconstruction. Select the cloud and choose Edit → Normals → Compute. Start with Auto for neighbourhood size and the default local model.

Use valid scan grids or sensor information for orientation when available. Without it, use the Minimum Spanning Tree orientation option. Check that directions are consistent around walls, arch and floor; one global +Z direction is unsuitable for all those surfaces.
Instructions:
Normal computation
Reconstruct the sample with output density enabled

Select the cloud with normals, open Plugins → PoissonRecon and enable output density as SF. Start with the installed defaults. Save the settings used. Increasing octree depth changes mesh detail and resource use; choose further changes from the sample’s actual result.
Remove unsupported mesh extensions

Select the output mesh. Under Properties → SF display params, raise the lower density threshold until unsupported extensions disappear while captured edges remain. This first changes visibility. Use Edit → Scalar fields → Filter by Value to create a mesh containing the retained triangles.

Inspect windows, door openings and the underside of the wheel arch. Density trimming can still leave surfaces filling areas that were never measured. Compare with the input cloud and remove or mark those fills.
Compare the mesh with the measured cloud

Select the preserved working cloud and the new mesh. Choose Tools → Distances → Cloud/Mesh dist. and click Compute. The initial preview statistics are approximate. Inspect the distance colours at curved and narrow features.
Record the affected areas and the scale of the deviations. These values describe mesh-to-cloud agreement; use the independent tape checks for agreement with the van.
Instructions:
Cloud-to-mesh distances
Repeat the accepted process for the useful body and door regions

Use the settings supported by the sample as a starting point, inspecting each region’s coverage and edge preservation. Keep the cloud available whenever a mesh smooths away a rib or returns a questionable curve.
If normals or reconstruction remain unreliable, retain the point cloud and proceed with sections from it.
Export the mesh and preserve the working project
Save the CloudCompare project as
nv200-04-mesh.bin
. Select each retained mesh and use File → Save to export OBJ for viewing and STL for build123d reference import. Keep door files separate and record their configuration.
Write the coordinate unit beside every OBJ/STL in
session-notes.txt
; these formats do not reliably carry that unit through every application. Preserve the full-detail version if creating a lighter viewing copy.
Extract sections at the furniture and body interfaces
Instructions:
CloudCompare cross-section tool
Open the section tool on the aligned reference cloud

Select the useful registered body clouds and choose Tools → Segmentation → Cross Section. Set the clipping box’s position, orientation and X/Y/Z extents numerically. Use a narrow slice that contains enough points without mixing nearby distinct surfaces.
Extract cross-van profiles at the critical locations

Place transverse slices at the rear opening, wheel-arch rear/front ends and crown, sliding-door posts, cabinet end/divider fitting positions and the cab-end cross-bench region. Record each slice position and thickness.
Use Export slice to create each slice entity in the DB tree. This button creates an entity inside CloudCompare; use File → Save later to create a file.
Extract horizontal clearance profiles

Create slices at the identified floor level, wheel-arch crown, bench/slat level, important cabinet shelf levels and the roof/rail interface. Keep height references explicit: the current slat top is 390 mm above the finished floor, and current metal floor is 18 mm lower than that floor datum.
Create longitudinal slices through wheel arches and roof curvature where they help distinguish the surfaces. Save screenshots showing each slice’s location in the whole van.
Generate profile polylines and inspect them

Use Extract envelope / Extract envelope(s), select the flat dimension and choose the required outline. Inspect the edge-length setting and resulting joins; stop outlines bridging separate panels or door openings. Keep the slice cloud alongside each derived line.
Extract multiple slices can repeat the operation along a chosen axis after one representative slice is correct. Record the spacing and thickness used.
Save the sections and their locations
Save the complete section project in
05-sections/nv200-sections.bin

. Select the useful polylines and export DXF. Keep slice clouds as PLY where useful. Name each file by orientation, location and configuration; include units and the positioning record in the handoff.
Package the scan for the assistant and optional Blender inspection
Inspect the mesh in Blender if useful

Import an OBJ or STL using Blender’s matching File → Import entry. Confirm a known length after import and apply the recorded unit interpretation. Inspect both sides of wheel arches, door clearances, roof joins and panel returns.
Prepare the handoff folder
Copy the optimised E57s, cleaned/aligned CloudCompare BIN, separate body/door meshes, DXF/PLY sections, session notes, measurement tables and target-location photos into
06-handoff
. Include representative screenshots and a list of uncertain / missing areas.
Keep the raw DP archives in the dated session folder. Provide them too when reconstruction needs revisiting.
Provide the files and the reconstruction task to the assistant

Ask the assistant to align the reference to our app’s vehicle coordinates, construct the measured floor/wheel arches/walls/pillars/roof/openings and separate doors, and compare that geometry with the scan and the independent measurements. State which trim/floor layers were present in each capture.
Assistant: reconstruct the measured van geometry in the campervan app
The assistant will add scan reference loading and reconstruct the measured body geometry in the app.
Instructions:
build123d reference and STEP import
Map units and physical references into the existing app coordinates

Confirm the export units using recorded dimensions, convert to millimetres once, and record the rigid coordinate transform. Match rear-opening Y = 0, left-to-right X and upward Z. Apply the measured finished-floor / metal-floor offset.
Construct the floor, wheel arches and lower body

Use the clouds and sections to reconstruct the actual floor boundary, both wheel arches down to metal-floor level, lower wall returns and rear corners. Retain corrugations or small features only where they affect furniture contact and clearance; record any simplification and its fit error.
Construct pillars, openings, roof and separate door components

Fit the sliding openings/posts, rear opening, wall taper, roof/rails/bows and the cab-end boundary. Use closed-door captures for the inward door profiles. Keep doors as separate moving parts and record which hinge/slide dimensions still need direct measurement.
Use automatic CAD surfacing where it proves helpful
For a difficult captured surface, evaluate automatic surfacing against the reference and the existing modelling approach.
QUICKSURFACE’s edition comparison
identifies the Pro automatic-freeform and STEP export capabilities. Confirm the required edition and actual cost before introducing a paid conversion step.
A measured mesh plus extracted sections can already support reconstruction. Any fitted CAD surface must be checked for deviations and for artificial bridges across unmeasured gaps.
Compare rebuilt geometry with the scan and the check distances
Produce an overlay / deviation inspection, repeat C01–C05 on the rebuilt geometry, and document maximum discrepancies at the furniture interfaces. Mark regions where scan coverage is incomplete.
Inspect the furniture fit in the app

Check long-bench and cabinet clearance at both arches and lower walls, rear drawer clearance with the hatch closed, cross-bench feet on the correct floor surface, cabinet roof clearance and sliding-door travel / access. Preserve the existing furniture dimensions unless a measured fit issue requires an agreed change.
Confirm the final construction measurements and templates
Recheck the specific interfaces before cutting fitted parts

Measure the cabinet rear/cab-end/divider profiles, bench arch clearance, cross-bench floor contact, rear corner and door clearance in the actual van at their intended positions. Record any difference from the rebuilt model beside the relevant interface.
Make full-size templates for irregular plywood edges

Use cardboard templates at the actual panel locations for wall, arch, pillar and roof profiles. Mark floor datum, front/rear and left/right on each template. Include the designed installation clearance and floor/lining thickness.
Feed confirmed corrections back into CAD and the cut list

Provide the template corrections and measured offsets to the assistant. Update affected geometry and cut profiles, then inspect the relevant pieces in the app and cut-list layout before purchasing or cutting fitted stock.
Keep a final record of the measured van model
Retain the dated raw / optimised captures, independent-check results, coordinate mapping, reconstruction settings and final template corrections.
Investigate a VR walkthrough of the interior for the HP Reverb G2, probably using Windows.
Create a full-size cardboard mock-up inside the van.
Source cardboard, painter's tape, knife and scissors.
Create interior mock-ups.
Try the layout and make adjustments.
Take final mock-up measurements and feed them back into CAD.
Finalise design after the mock-up.
Confirm final measurements.
Complete final materials check.
Ensure the inventory includes fasteners and finishing materials such as paint or stain.
Finalise the bill of materials, including tools and consumables.
Squabs
Make five removable covers for the existing mattress.

Make five covers with two faces, four rectangular sides, a concealed #5 coil zip along one long side, and a small fabric pocket over the closed zip pull. Use the same cloth on both faces so you can turn the cushions over. Put your fitted sheet over the assembled bed.
This method hides the zip behind two fabric folds. You will see two lines of stitching alongside them. Use a standard zipper foot for this construction. The pocket in these steps hides the zip pull.
Learn the terms you will use while sewing
Right side:
the fabric surface you want outside.
Wrong side:
the surface against the foam. Put
right sides together
by placing the outside surfaces against each other. A
raw edge
is an edge you cut. A
seam allowance
is the cloth between the raw edge and your stitches. Here, you will sew the structural seams 15 mm from the raw edge.
Boxing:
the four sides of the cover.
Baste:
hold pieces together with tape or temporary long stitches.
Backstitch:
sew backwards for two or three stitches to secure the end of a seam.
Zigzag:
a stitch that moves from side to side; you will use it along cut edges to reduce fraying.
Selvedges:
the two finished edges running along a fabric roll. They may have printing, tiny holes or a stiff strip. Keep those strips outside your pattern pieces when measuring the usable fabric width.

Sew the four sides into a ring

Arrange solid long side, short side 1, zip side and short side 2 around the top face. Put neighbouring ends right sides together. Align their top and bottom raw edges. On the right-backrest cover, each panel is
130 mm high
At each join, sew
15 mm from the short raw end

and stopping

Tape the top face to the side ring
Put the top face right side up. Place the ring against its edges with right sides together. Match the piece labels, edge midpoints and four marked 15 mm corner intersections.

Tape one edge at a time inside the allowance. At each corner, fold the neighbouring side's loose allowance away from the edge you are about to sew. Match the marked seam intersections. If the lengths differ, check the cut sizes and corner marks before stitching.
Sew the top face to the ring
Fit the ordinary foot and set straight stitch to
3 mm
. Sew each edge on its
15 mm line
, starting at one marked corner intersection and ending at the next. Backstitch two or three stitches at the beginning and end. Support the loose fabric on the table and let the machine feed it.

At each corner, stop and reposition the loose allowances before sewing the next edge. Keep the adjacent side out from under the needle. Check that the two stitch lines meet at the same intersection and leave no corner hole. Inspect the first corner for trapped cloth and a gap between the stitch lines before sewing the other three.
Open the zip and attach the bottom face
Open the zip at least halfway. Match the bottom face's labels to the top, then tape it to the ring, right sides together. Match the edge midpoints and marked corner intersections.
Sew its four edges at
15 mm
, using the same corner-to-corner sequence as the top. Keep the opposite face and loose side fabric out of each seam. Leave the zip open so you can turn the cover through it.
Turn the cover right side out

Inspect the inside seams for missed layers and corner holes. Repair those seams before turning the cover. Reach through the zip and pull the cloth through. Push out the corners with your fingers or the rounded end of a smooth wooden spoon.
Open and close the zip. Check you can reach its pull under the pocket. Remove loose threads and visible tape. Keep the corner allowances intact for the first fitting.
Insert the foam

Open the zip to its stops. Compress the right-backrest foam with your hands and feed it through the opening. Work the cover over the far corners, then over the near corners. Move the fabric over the foam a little at a time. Keep the foam's bonded layers aligned.

If the cloth grips the foam, wrap the foam in a clean thin plastic sheet with one end left accessible at the zip. Slide the cover over it, then pull the plastic out. Smooth the foam into the corners with flat hands.
Check this cover before making the other four

Compress the foam by hand to bring the zip sides together, then close the zip. Check for a flat foam block, filled corners, smooth faces and seams sitting at the edges. Remove and refit the cover once.
If the zip needs force or the foam bows, check your actual foam measurements and 15 mm seams. If those match, reduce the 10 mm fit deduction: try
5 mm total
on the next pattern, or
zero
if the foam barely compresses. A shallower seam can add room, but it also leaves less cloth beside the stitches. Check that alteration with the tutor before recutting the panel.

If the cloth bags, check for stretched fabric or seams shallower than 15 mm. Record the correction and revise all five cut-list rows before cutting more. Keep the successful first cover beside you while sewing the remaining four.
Fit all five cushions in the van
Arrange the pieces as seats and backrests, then make the
bed using the layout in 2.1.5. Put on your fitted sheet. Lie across the joins and sit on each seat. Check that you can lift the seats, reach the zips and remove the covers.

Use the slatted bed base already in the design. Lift the cushions after sleeping and let the undersides dry before packing bedding against them. Check the underside for dampness during the first few nights;

explains the need for airflow under foam.
Record the pattern and washing settings

Record each cushion's actual foam dimensions, final fit deduction, cut pieces, zip position, needle, machine model and stitch settings. Keep the fabric care instructions and a labelled scrap with this guide.
